NEW_HEADLINE_METRIC: P(complete required path survives into the final packet | complete required path exists in the working set) -- individual bridge/terminal retention can look acceptable while the packet holds fragments of INCOMPATIBLE paths

FINDING_1_dominant_failure_is_WRONG_PATH.reading: Of required records that ARE present in the working set but do not reach the packet, ~64% are lost because S2 prefers a COMPETING complete path. The selector is not failing to see the evidence and is not mis-scoring individual records -- it is assembling a packet from fragments of incompatible paths.

FINDING_2_path_coherent_composition_clos.reading: Admitting the highest-ranked COMPLETE path's records first -- changing nothing about ranking, retrieval, graph, or working set -- raises selected CES 0.323 -> 0.528, more than doubles bridge retention (0.183 -> 0.423) and more than doubles complete-path retention (0.217 -> 0.503). This is the single largest selection-side lever found.

FINDING_3_redundancy_is_NOT_the_problem.reading: Suppressing duplicate structural signatures eliminates redundancy entirely (0.57 -> 0.00) and makes selected CES slightly WORSE. Redundancy collision accounts for only 3.1% of failures. A diversity/dedup fix is ruled out.

FINDING_4_role_reservation_helps_but_onl.reading: Reserving one slot per runtime-inferred role recovers 19.3% of the gap, almost entirely through TERMINAL retention (0.497 -> 0.614). Bridge retention slightly DROPS (0.183 -> 0.168), because a reserved terminal slot can displace the bridge. Role balance is a real but secondary factor, and less than half as valuable as path coherence.

FINDING_5_large_selection_side_headroom_.reading: Perfect selection on the SAME G2/E1 working sets reaches 0.793 vs the current 0.323. The working sets already contain far more usable evidence than S2 extracts. Selection, not availability, is where the remaining value is.

IMPLICATION_FOR_G2_VS_TYPED_PATH.caveat: Approximate: the S3 diagnostic pools tasks with a non-empty working set and the ladder pools all tasks, so this is an indicative comparison, not a certified head-to-head. A promoted mechanism would need its own frozen gate and a like-for-like run.
IMPLICATION_FOR_G2_VS_TYPED_PATH.reading: The S3 baseline (0.323) closely matches the G2 ladder mean (0.312), so the arms are comparable. A path-coherent composition would put G2 at ~0.528, decisively ABOVE typed path's ~0.377. This is the first evidence that the graph substrate can overtake the simpler mechanism -- but ONLY once packet composition becomes path-aware.

frozen_decision_rule_outcome.branch_taken: 'if S1/S2_role_reserved/S3_path_coherent recovers a large share of the S4 gap -> the defect is packet composition, and a composition fix may finally let G2 overtake typed path'
frozen_decision_rule_outcome.verdict: The defect IS packet composition, specifically PATH COHERENCE. Not record ranking, not redundancy, not capacity, not tie-breaking.

status_board.G2_graph_traversal: IMPROVED; may overtake typed path IF composition becomes path-aware

S3_RESULT.what_is_NOT_promoted: S1/S2/S3 are diagnostic arms. S3_path_coherent naively takes the top complete path and is not a mechanism -- it has no policy for competing complete paths of equal rank, no safety bounds, and no protocol. Promotion requires its own frozen gate.

decision_rule_frozen.even_oracle_barely_helps: if S4 barely improves on the same working sets -> G2's extra complexity still is not paying for itself; keep G1_TYPED_PATH as the architecture
decision_rule_frozen.simple_fix_recovers_most: if S1/S2_role_reserved/S3_path_coherent recovers a large share of the S4 gap -> the defect is packet composition, and a composition fix may finally let G2 overtake typed path

key_separation: record RANKING is separated from packet COMPOSITION: S2 may be assigning reasonable per-record scores while composing a poor packet.

S1_diversity.selector: suppress near-duplicate structural signatures, then unchanged S2

S2_role_reserved.selector: reserve 1 identity + 1 bridge + 1 terminal by RUNTIME-inferred role, fill remaining 3 with unchanged S2

S3_path_coherent.selector: admit all records supporting the highest-ranked COMPLETE path first, then fill

only_treatment_variable: the selector that turns a working set into the six-record packet
question: Given a working set in which the required bridge and terminal evidence are ALREADY present, why does S2 select the wrong six records?
why_now: G2-v4E's grammar_v4 removed the availability bottleneck strongly enough to expose the next one. At cal_3000/M50, bridge working-set survival is 1.000 while P(bridge selected | in working set) is 0.015; terminal survival 0.747 with retention 0.268. Bridge acquisition therefore comes OFF the critical path -- the evidence is reaching the working set and dying in selection.
